candidates.question: With an unchanged generator, all frozen synthetic samples retained and fixed total real/synthetic exposure, can temporal organization reduce across-realization utility variability without class AP sacrifice?
candidates.evidence_basis: Stage20B instability motivates an integration question, but does not isolate exposure timing as its cause.
candidates.minimality: One conceptual training-time axis; no new generator, image score, learned gate or sample ranking.
candidates.risk: Schedule search on the existing final_eval would be post-hoc tuning; changing total exposure would confound integration with quantity.
candidates.selector_boundary: No dropping samples, quality-based order, class suppression or zero exposure; same complete frozen input population.

candidates.question: Can training-time uncertainty regulate synthetic gradient contribution without excluding samples?
candidates.evidence_basis: No calibrated uncertainty evidence in Stage20B.
candidates.minimality: Less minimal: an uncertainty definition, calibration and scale introduce additional assumptions.
candidates.risk: Per-sample zero/near-zero weights or quality rank is a soft selector and overlaps BootstrapGuard; uncertainty can favor easy examples.
candidates.selector_boundary: No permanent sample gate/rank/topK; all samples and nonzero exposure retained. Merely calling scores 'weights' is insufficient separation.

candidates.question: Can an integration rule avoid class-asymmetric harm without selecting samples or permanently disabling a class?
candidates.evidence_basis: V2 degradation is concentrated in Black, but Stage17A degradation was stronger in Flash; no universal class rule.
candidates.minimality: Potentially small, but a class rule needs independent train-only evidence rather than fitting these APs.
candidates.risk: Post-hoc Black-only penalty/suppression would tune to observed final_eval; changed per-class exposure confounds mechanism.
candidates.selector_boundary: Retain both classes and complete sample sets; no Black filtering or final_eval-driven class weights.

candidates.question: Can an explicit training-time consistency constraint improve robustness to synthetic variation?
candidates.evidence_basis: Prediction inconsistency was not measured as the failure cause.
candidates.minimality: Requires a transformation/target-consistency assumption not supplied by current evidence.
candidates.risk: Wrong or weak labels can be reinforced; extra forwards/targets and hyperparameters muddy compute attribution.
candidates.selector_boundary: All samples retained; no consistency-based acceptance/rejection.

candidates.question: Can real/synthetic distribution information control joint optimization without post-generation sample ranking?
candidates.evidence_basis: Historical concentration diagnostics do not prove distribution mismatch causes V2 failure.
candidates.minimality: Highest conceptual burden: representation, distribution and aggregation choices.
candidates.risk: A nearest-real/guardrail score used for per-sample exclusion would reproduce selector behavior; teacher-space and domain assumptions unresolved.
candidates.selector_boundary: Training-level aggregate integration only; no novelty/fidelity quality score or pool filtering.

primary_question: With an unchanged generator, all frozen synthetic samples retained and fixed total real/synthetic exposure, can temporal organization reduce across-realization utility variability without class AP sacrifice?
